title: Rust: common windows and finite radio resources
description:
Integrate rust/lichen-hal/src/lib.rs Radio/Concentrator capabilities, rust/lichen-node/src/tdma_scheduler.rs and rust/lichen-gateway/src/tdma_fsm.rs into bounded CCP2 control/data opportunities. Common CH0 listening, activation/expiry, retuning, clock uncertainty and actual RX/TX resources must be explicit. Hold profile 0x01 at its specified SF10 parameters throughout a generation.

HPC8 execution policy: Code, test, or schema changes require three independent correctness, security, and robustness reviews; file and fix all findings and re-review. Use independent oracles, never weakened legacy tests or self-generated expected results. Preserve upstream Yggdrasil addressing, radio-owned identity, best-effort custody, baseline SCHC, and the human-only OSCORE/EDHOC security edit bar. External actions, hardware/RF operations, and port access require scoped explicit permission and applicable bench safety checks. Research may conclude no-go; an authorization gate requires affirmative, recorded approval for its actual scope. Dependency closure and decomposition are not permission. No speculative activation, including deferred portability or experimental modes.
design: Compose rust.04 grants, rust.06 costs and rust.12 synchronization without a new scheduler framework. Existing Concentrator type names and tunable settings are not evidence of implemented simultaneous reception. Do not invent cadence, adaptive controllers or mandatory hopping. Preserve radio-owned identity, upstream addressing, baseline SCHC/security and custody semantics; hardware resources here are test inputs, not RF qualification.
acceptance_criteria: Consume vectors.04/.06 using independent finite-resource event traces. Verify a single radio never occupies two channels, multiple RX chains do not imply multiple TX chains, common control returns fit complete exchanges, and invalid/expired schedules stop data TX. Test restricted passbands, demodulator limits and density/load changes without channel/profile changes. Exercise production scheduler/HAL boundaries in node/gateway tests; run feature-qualified tests, core/HAL no-default-feature checks, fmt and clippy.
